title: Phone Number Extractor: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Phone Number Extractor](/phone-number-extractor) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Find and list every phone number in a block of text. Enter your text to search and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Find every phone number hidden in a block of text — emails, documents, chat logs, web pages — and list them one per line. It recognises common formats: international numbers with a + country code, numbers in parentheses, and numbers separated by spaces, dashes or dots. Anything with 7 to 15 digits that looks like a phone number is picked up; short numbers such as years and order numbers are ignored. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Phone Number Extractor

Start by typing or pasting your text to search. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste the text that contains the phone numbers.
2. Read the list — one number per line, in the order they appear.
3. Copy the list into a spreadsheet or contact list.

## How it works

The [Phone Number Extractor](/phone-number-extractor) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. From “Call the office on (415) 555-0132 or mobile +1 650-555-0147” it extracts (415) 555-0132 and +1 650-555-0147 — two numbers. The fax number 415.555.0199 is also found, making three in total. Try the same figures in the [Phone Number Extractor](/phone-number-extractor) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Text to search: Call the office on (415) 555-0132 or mobile +1 650-555-0147. The old fax 415.555.0199 is no longer in service.), the [Phone Number Extractor](/phone-number-extractor) returns Phone numbers found: (415) 555-0132 +1 650-555-0147 415.555.0199, Count: 3. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Word Counter](/word-counter) is worth a look before you finish.

## What counts as a phone number

A phone number is a run of 7 to 15 digits, optionally starting with a + country code, with spaces, dashes, dots or parentheses in between. That covers US numbers (415) 555-0132, international numbers such as +44 20 7946 0958, and plain digit strings. Short digit runs — years like 2026, order numbers, prices — are ignored because they have too few digits to be a phone number.

## Cleaning up the results

Extracted numbers keep their original formatting, so the same number can appear twice in different formats. Before importing into a contacts app, normalise them: strip spaces, dashes and parentheses, and add the country code if it is missing. A quick pass with the Remove Accents tool is not needed here — phone numbers are digits only — but a spreadsheet's find-and-replace will tidy the formatting fast.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Numbers need at least 7 digits to be picked up — short extensions are ignored.
- Check the count against what you expect; a missing number may be split across two lines in the source.
- Always confirm a number with the person before using it for anything important.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which phone number formats are recognised?

International numbers with a + country code, numbers in parentheses like (415) 555-0132, and numbers separated by spaces, dashes or dots. The number needs 7 to 15 digits in total. Try it with your own numbers in the [Phone Number Extractor](/phone-number-extractor) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why was a number missed?

Usually because it has fewer than 7 digits, or because it is split across a line break in the source text. Join the lines first and try again. Try it with your own numbers in the [Phone Number Extractor](/phone-number-extractor) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does it validate the numbers?

No — it finds text that looks like a phone number; it does not check whether the number is real or in service. Always verify before calling or messaging. Try it with your own numbers in the [Phone Number Extractor](/phone-number-extractor) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Phone Number Extractor?

Just Text to search. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
